cases.name: one blob, one drop
cases.why: a chain runs through every mote missing the colour that was dropped, and a whole row of them is one drop

cases.name: a wall of the wrong colour
cases.why: cyan already holds blue, so the chain neither takes it nor crosses it - which is the whole of what makes colour a decision here

cases.name: two blobs the wash cannot cross between
a burst under a stack
cases.why: gravity only pulls down, so a well collapses when a wash reaches something a drop never could - and the wash is read before the fall

cases.name: a pure mote finished by two bursts
cases.why: the red between a yellow blob and a magenta blob takes blue from one and green from the other, and bursts without anybody ever dropping on it - which is what a pure mote is for

cases.name: nothing on this board wants what the well deals
cases.why: proved unsolvable rather than timed out, which is the difference between a level that is broken and one that is too big

cases.name: a column with no room and a procession that opens badly
cases.why: the only mote yellow lacks is blue, so red and green both come to rest on the brim and the search will not count either - par is the fewest drops that empty a well without ever breaching the line

cases.name: a well that has to be emptied from the top down
cases.why: every drop lands on a column top, so what is buried is reached by the wash or not at all

cases.name: a shipped shape
cases.why: five rows, three regions and a scattering of pure motes - the shape a chapter actually authors
